General.Description:
Thomas Aldridge founded his first company at nineteen with borrowed money and a vision so specific that early investors laughed him out of three consecutive pitch meetings. By thirty-five he was a billionaire. By forty-five he had sold that company, founded two more, and begun quietly reshaping the global infrastructure of renewable energy logistics. He was also, by every account, one of the most difficult people anyone who knew him had ever worked with.

Patricia Rourke's biography of Aldridge is the authorised account of a genuinely complex figure — a man of visionary intelligence and deep interpersonal blindness, whose inability to hear no led as often to transformative breakthroughs as to spectacular internal failures. Drawing on five years of access including candid interviews with Aldridge himself, his co-founders, estranged family members, and the employees who left and the ones who stayed, Rourke constructs a portrait of innovation that refuses easy hagiography.

The Visionary is not a business book dressed up as biography. It is a sustained inquiry into the nature of obsession — what it produces, what it costs, and whether the products are worth the price.

Authoritative, balanced, and compulsively readable.
